gaps.spec_claim: Returns a string of length len(text). For every character position i in the returned string: if text[i] lay within a comment  determined by the comment syntax rules of the language identified by lang_key  the returned character is a space; otherwise, the returned character equals text[i]. Comment syntax rules: languages whose line-comment prefix is '#' use line comments from '#' to end of line. All other languages use C-family comment syntax: line comments from '//' to end of line, and block comments delimited by '/*' and '*/'. Characters within string literals (single-quoted, double-quoted, or triple-quoted) are never interpreted as comment-starting sequences; string literals whose delimiters contain the comment prefix do not trigger comment removal.
gaps.actual_behavior:
After executing the code block, the program reaches the return statement and returns a string. The returned string is obtained from the original input by replacing certain characters with spaces. Specifically, let `text` be the original input string, `n = len(text)`, and `result` initially be `list(text)`. After the loops, for each index j from 0 to n-1, `result[j]` is set to a space if j falls inside a string literal or comment and `text[j]` is not a newline; otherwise `result[j]` remains `text[j]`. A string literal is a substring starting with a single or double quote character and ending with a matching quote (backslash escaping is handled so that an escaped quote does not end the literal). The opening quote character itself is not replaced; the closing quote is replaced. A hash comment starts with `#` and ends at the next newline (all characters including `#` are replaced). A C-style line comment starts with `//` and ends at the next newline (the two slashes and all following characters are replaced). A C-style block comment starts with `/*` and ends with the next `*/` (all characters between and including the markers are replaced). In all replacements, newline characters `
` are never replaced, i.e., they remain as newlines. After all characters have been processed, `i == n`. The variables `lang_cfg`, `comment_prefix`, and `is_hash_comment` are unchanged from their values computed earlier. The function returns `"".join(result)`. No exceptions are raised.

gaps.trigger_condition: The code treats any single quote as the end of a string literal, so a triple-quoted string is prematurely closed. As a result, a '#' character inside a triple-quoted string (e.g., """# not a comment""") is no longer inside a string literal after the first two quotes are consumed, leading to it being recognized as a line comment and replaced with a space. The specification requires that characters within string literals are never interpreted as comment-starting sequences, and triple-quoted strings must be respected.
